chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from Uthman ibn Thabit, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him), 'O Ali, I advise you regarding your soul concerning certain qualities, so preserve them from me - O Allah, help him -'

As for the first, it is truthfulness - never let a lie be spoken from your mouth. The second is piety - never act treacherously. The third is fearing Allah as though you see Him. The fourth is crying out of fear of Allah - for each tear a mansion will be built for you in Paradise. The fifth is spending your wealth and tears for your religion. The sixth is adhering to my sunnah in my prayer, my fasting, and my charity.

As for my prayer, it is fifty-one [rak'ahs]; as for my fasting, it is three days in every month, in its beginning, middle, and end; as for my charity, it is to spare no effort until it is said that you have been extravagant, while you have not been extravagant.

And I bid you to maintain the nightly prayer, maintain the nightly prayer, maintain the nightly prayer! And I bid you to maintain the midday prayer, maintain the midday prayer, maintain the midday prayer! I bid you to recite the Qur'an in every condition.

And I bid you to raise your hands in supplication and then turn them back [towards yourself]. I bid you to brush your teeth during every ablution and prayer. And I bid you to [espouse] beautiful moral traits so inculcate them [in yourself], and I warn you against evil traits so eschew them.
Then if you do not act upon what I advise you [herewith], then do not blame anyone but yourself [for the consequences].
ai.seo_question: What are the six qualities the Prophet advised Ali to adopt for spiritual success?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the intimate spiritual mentorship between the Prophet and Imam Ali, framing piety through six specific virtues: truthfulness, asceticism, God-consciousness, weeping, spending, and adherence to the Prophet's unique sunnah. It provides a detailed blueprint for devotional practice, emphasizing the Prophet's specific prayer units, monthly fasting schedule, and the critical importance of night and midday prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt's specific interpretation of worship.
